claim: The llm-d-routing-sidecar GitHub repo is archived and deprecated; its code was moved into the llm-d-inference-scheduler repository under cmd/pd_sidecar and pkg/sidecar, and all future development happens there.
stance_target: current location of P/D sidecar source code
quoted_support: The code of the routing sidecar has been moved to the llm-d-inference-scheduler repository, under the cmd/pd_sidecar and pkg/sidecar directories. This repository is deprecated and shall soon be archived.

claim: The routing sidecar is a reverse proxy that forwards requests to whichever prefill worker is named in the x-prefiller-host-port HTTP header, in host:port format.
stance_target: sidecar core mechanism / coupling to backend addressing
quoted_support: This project provides a reverse proxy redirecting incoming requests to the prefill worker specified in the x-prefiller-host-port HTTP request header.

claim: SSRF protection in the sidecar is opt-in (disabled by default) via --enable-ssrf-protection, and when enabled it watches a specific InferencePool CRD to build a host/IP allowlist from matching pods; requests to hosts outside the allowlist return HTTP 403.
stance_target: the sidecar's SSRF defense is architecturally tied to Kubernetes InferencePool/pod-watch
scope_conditions: feature added in PR #49, merged Jul 18, 2025
quoted_support: When enabled, it watches a specific InferencePool resource and maintains an allowlist of valid prefill targets based on pods matching the InferencePool selectors... Requests to unauthorized targets return HTTP 403 Forbidden.

claim: The SSRF allowlist tracks hosts/IPs only, not ports -- any port on an allowed host is permitted once that host is in the allowlist.
quoted_support: The allowlist tracks hosts/IPs only (not specific ports), so any port on an allowed host is permitted.

claim: For automatic namespace injection, the Kubernetes deployment pattern for the sidecar uses the Downward API to populate INFERENCE_POOL_NAMESPACE from metadata.namespace, tying configuration directly to a live Kubernetes pod spec.
stance_target: sidecar deployment model assumes Kubernetes pod semantics
quoted_support: For automatic namespace injection in Kubernetes deployments, use the downward API: ... env: - name: INFERENCE_POOL_NAMESPACE valueFrom: fieldRef: fieldPath: metadata.namespace

claim: When SSRF protection is disabled (the default), all prefill targets named in x-prefiller-host-port are allowed for backward compatibility, meaning a non-Kubernetes deployment can run the sidecar functionally but without the allowlist defense.
stance_target: non-k8s backends can use the sidecar today only by forgoing SSRF protection
quoted_support: When disabled (default), all targets are allowed for backward compatibility.

claim: The sidecar's quick-start requires vLLM instances started with kv-transfer-config using NixlConnector and kv_role=kv_both, and the NIXL side-channel host/port are set via VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST/PORT env vars, independent of any Kubernetes API.
stance_target: KV-transfer networking requirement is orthogonal to Kubernetes
scope_conditions: example uses podman with --network host and GPU device passthrough

claim: The sidecar supports three P/D connector backends selectable via --connector: nixl and lmcache (both deprecated) and nixlv2 (current default), with nixlv2 becoming default in PR #53.
quoted_support: the P/D connector being used. Either nixl, nixlv2 or lmcache (default "nixl") ... Note: lmcache and nixl connectors are deprecated. Use nixlv2

claim: Latest tagged release of llm-d-routing-sidecar was v0.3.0 on Sep 25, 2025, before the repo's archival on Feb 3, 2026.
